outcome: Help approved teams create Arabic/English drafts, subtitles, captions, metadata, clips and adaptations faster while preserving editorial voice, rights and cultural meaning.
overview: Broadcasters, streamers and publishers across the Gulf serve bilingual audiences, yet subtitling, dubbing scripts, metadata and social versions are still produced largely by hand, so Arabic releases trail the original and quality varies by team. This solution puts AI-assisted transcription, translation and adaptation inside a rights-aware editorial workflow: every draft carries provenance, terminology follows approved glossaries, accessibility checks run automatically, and an editor approves each output before release. A 6–10 week pilot on a licensed asset set targets roughly 30% faster approved turnaround with less rework — editorial voice, cultural review and human approval preserved throughout, and every released output traceable.

benefits.source: Workflow design — the publishing gate captures provenance and approval per output

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); source assets, drafts and approval records remain in the customer tenancy in the reference designs

notFor.situation: Source content is not licensed for derivative works or AI-assisted processing
notFor.why: The workflow only operates on assets with clear rights metadata; unlicensed sources create infringement exposure no tooling can remove

notFor.situation: No editorial review capacity to approve generated drafts
notFor.why: Every output requires human approval before release; without reviewers the pipeline stalls or unreviewed content ships

notFor.situation: Fully automated publishing with no human in the loop is the goal
notFor.why: The design keeps editorial voice, cultural meaning and rights under human authority by intent; removing approval is out of scope

Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, media-workflow engineer, localisation specialist; customer editorial owner, rights owner, accessibility lead, security approver · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
